question: Why is GPT-2 used as the reference model for memory-bandwidth-limited workloads, and how does its generation process create that bottleneck?
answer_key_points: GPT-2 is a decoder-only transformer that produces text autoregressively — each new token depends on all the tokens generated before it, so one full forward pass is needed per token.
Every token requires streaming the whole set of weights out of memory (e.g., roughly 3 GB for a 1.5B-parameter model stored in FP16), while the actual arithmetic is only a matrix-vector product.
That gives an arithmetic intensity of roughly 1 FLOP per byte moved, so performance is capped by memory bandwidth rather than by available compute.
The serial, token-at-a-time dependency prevents the kind of batched dense math that keeps compute units busy, unlike bidirectional encoder models such as BERT that process context all at once.
